title: Ordinary coefficient-system compact-support transport
statement: For a prime l, finite normed coefficient extensions E and F of Q_l, and a Q_l-algebra embedding i : E → F, use the actual lifted finite quotient-ring towers and the scalar maps induced by i. Construct their whole ring-system map and exact module and derived scalar restriction. For each scheme map f, construct the section-normalized restriction/direct-image square and its inverse pullback mate, prove that mate invertible by coefficient evaluation, and derive its exact localization. The proper direct-image mate and open-extension inverse mate are invertible. For a compactification c, the whole-system compact-support functor is open extension followed by derived proper direct image; assemble the two restriction squares, and define its scalar-extension projection by the specified scalar adjunction mate. The generic right-derived comparison on complexes and its naturality are retained as auxiliary constructions. All objects, signatures and bodies are those previously in the parent module, unchanged. Coefficient towers, geometric operations, compactifications and scalar adjunctions are from the recorded statement dependencies.
proof_origin: K1 splits the already stated ordinary construction from the limit construction for the per-file compile limit. All original public names, signatures and non-theorem bodies stay unchanged. The pullback inverse-mate proof is completed by normalized coefficient evaluation; the other transferred proofs remain complete.

proof.text: The finite scalar maps commute with quotient transitions by the integral scalar quotient-map theorem. Applying constant sheafification gives the commutative-system morphism; exact restriction and the given scalar adjunction produce the whole-system restriction and scalar data. Define the universal right-derived unit using its homotopy-quotient comparisons; its naturality follows from the existing derived-unit naturality equation.

Naturality of constant coefficient sheaves makes the geometric coefficient square commute. Module direct-image compositors and congruence along that square construct the unique section-normalized restriction/pushforward isomorphism. Its inverse has the specified pullback mate. Canonical restriction/evaluation comparisons and coefficient-map naturality meet the normalized evaluation theorem hypotheses. This proves invertibility at every coefficient level, and the faithful underlying additive sheaf functor shows evaluation is conservative. Thus the whole inverse mate is invertible.

Exact localization of the pullback comparison defines its derived version. The continuous scalar-resolution theorem supplies the resolution hypothesis for the generic derived-mate criterion, proving the proper-image comparison invertible. Scalar restriction preserves the derived open essential image; the open adjunction counit criterion and supported inverse-mate criterion prove the open comparison invertible. Compose the proper and open squares along the actual compactification, and take the scalar adjunction mate to define systemProjection.
